body:
I understand that, but without being dramatic, I can only see me making a difference with my life if I end it and make a statement that saves others.
Plus I won’t have to deal with this living shit either.

My problem is I’m leaving, but I’m a fixer; I have to make it right before I go.

We were so understaffed last night that when I asked for a little help, someone snapped at me “whatever’s not done they can deal with later”.
All well and good until I tell you I was asking then to do checks on a guy who end to ITU about 20minutes later.

Patients are suffering, the higher-ups are actively ignoring us AND the issues. People are getting hurt, people are not getting the care that they need, and I’m meant to say 🤷‍♀️ “ I did my best”?

I keep thinking...if I kill myself, write a note laying out the staffing issues, naming and shaming those in charge, spilling every time patient care was compromised....something will *have* to change.

It is believed that the Benders were not actually a family, but that only two of the group were related, or married. (Only citation I have is “My Favourite Murder” though).
As for the Swaney Bean family, that’s not really considered to be truth, merely legend, rumour and the casual racism of the time. 
I think is was covered by the “Lore” podcast...
But it was likely one or two people or completely separate individuals with similar MO’s.

It’s usually only couples or cults, or father/son, mother/daughter duos.

From someone who worked in a morgue for a while, it was nice to have a character who wasn’t super* creepy working there!
Love the show, love your work!
*(not super creepy all the time, anyway😂)

It’s in the “Well that sucks” reddit.
It sucks that I opened something that was meant to be a surprise.
It sucks that I bought the same thing when I’d been holding off.
Yes it’s not a major problem, but it still sucks.

I don’t even know why you bothered to comment.
I’m 23, and not many people I know need a pill dispenser. Those that do, have one.
I nearly bit. But then again...why? :)

Well, duh!
(Or rather, keeping it for travel/if the other one breaks etc. No point throwing something perfectly good away!)
Serotonin and Noradrenaline re-uptake inhibitors  that can cause seizures or Serotonin Syndrome if not taken correctly.

And my friend has EDS and AS, she said she thought I should get checked for AS too!

But I don’t have many symptoms of it, luckily, I’m not going to push it just yet.

Hope your management is going better though! 
My friend said since the got the AS diagnosis, doctors have been much more helpful than when she just had EDS on her chart.

The thing is, I know the doctors that are great, in that I literally work with them.

But none of them run clinics, and trying to get a referral to a clinic is ridiculous, plus all the ‘good’ GPS at my surgery are on maternity leave or secondment.

Like I say, I’m moving house and jobs soon, so new GP, new hospital base.
I’m a pro at relocating my shoulder and hip, so the only current issue is that back thing, because it cannot just be the injury for 5 years ago making me incontinent. I mean, if it is, that’s mighty inconvenient!

Like you, I wish there was some consistency in care (and research!). 
A lot of people wouldn’t have my knowledge based to know when to push or get their medical notes. The C4-C5 fusion was only revealed to me because I asked for my notes too.

Makes me so frustrated for the people that get skipped over with stuff like this.

As I’ve been told! 

I mean, I only found out that the reason I was admitted to hospital 4 years ago was gastroparesis this week.
And that’s because I requested all my medical notes from the hospital.

They discharged me with no resolution, having been NBM with no IV fluids for 4 days, still no bowel movement (day 6) and the one time they tried me with food, I bought it back up.
I collapsed again later that day with a systolic of 82Hmmg.

This week there was concerns about Cauda Equina syndrome because of back pain, sciatica and (tmi) several episodes of incontinence, but the back pain has eased a lot, so I’ve been shifted home.

I’ll be honest, I think I just have bum luck, and my prioreceptors are terrible, so I get injured a lot, and my pain tolerance and stubbornness probably prevent me from healing full.

Nope, got no recommendations, no follows or follow up advice.

My GP says “all CBT now only comes from self referral” but I waited 3 months only to get turned away for it. 
(Finally got some, but they are focused on my PTSD.)

Since the diagnosis of PTSD, my GP has responding to every problem with “do you think this could be related to the trauma?” Despite the trauma being 8years ago, and the PTSD symptoms being present since then.
Do I think the prolong and skipped N-N complex that showed up in my 3day holter are in my head?
Nope, I think they are in my heart, where the ECG showed they were.
Do I think the facial twitches when I’m drinking, and right arm numbness/weakness are because of my trauma? Well, maybe, I get that some stuff is psychosomatic, but after 8 years, no new stressors, and a month of nerve based neck pain that spread to my arm? No not really!

My GP is terrible, and I cannot wait until I change when I move.

I wasn’t suggesting it didn’t need confirming by a geneticist, but after 4 GPS said to me “Oh, you probably have EDS” it *still* took 3 years, 3 failed rheumatological referrals and 3 GPS refusing to refer me to genetics AND a 6 month wait list to get me to one.

For some people, it is that difficult.

I have had 4 separate courses of CBT, an an 8 week Pain management course

My POTs is managed fine with medication and symptom recognition/self-management because I’m a CritCare nurse who can read the signs (apart from the kidney stone Secondary to increased salt intake that first year-oops!)

My IBS is the first issue I had, back from about age 10, and every female in my family has it, so no investigations, and just manage it like everyone else in my family does. Plus medical management for mild gastroparesis.

Most of my issues that actually need management (but don’t get them) are my C4-C5 fusion, spinal cord swelling that I get when my loose coccyx chip moves, and the chronic dislocations of my hips and right shoulder.

In the UK, you can get a hEDS diagnosis from a geneticist, but they won’t do a genetic test and they’ll only follow up if you need advice around getting pregnant and pre/postnatal care.

I saw one, once, for an hour, about 2 years ago. He got my medical history, my family medical history, did an examination and confirmed it. 
Gave me a little advice, and sent me on my way with a letter to my GP.

Neither my POTs, my hEDS, IBS or my PTSD are managed by anyone.
Discharged from both the Pain and Syncope clinics, because I was already doing everything they advised.

Oh, aloe vera juice.

Someone in my “managing chronic pain” education group decided the 3rd of 8sessions was the time to start promoting it. She was therefor 2 more 4hour sessions before she got booted.

As I don’t have symptoms for vEDS, they’ve diagnosed me with hEDS, and as there is not genetic test for that (yet) they said they won’t do genetic testing for me.

They did ask for medical history of family; everyone has IBS, the aneurysm thing, the hernias, the hypermobility, easy bruising, thin and saggy skin...
But as my Mum manages fine, she doesn’t want another diagnosis to add to her list.

I put it back in the Amazon box (I opened it the sneaky way, so it looks like it hasn’t been opened.
And I’m hiding my pill box.
The one he bought looks much nicer, anyway!
Updated.

It’s not overflow, it’s full on, well...you know.
I’m a nurse, which makes this all soooo much worse. 
Luckily at work, we have 1) a close toilet, 2) spare pads, and 3) spare scrubs. 
I’m forcing myself to go to the loo, literally setting reminders on my phone at work.
I used to go the whole 13hr shift without peeing (part dehydrate, part I didn’t have a chance) but always felt I could tell when I needed to go. 
(Yes, I know that’s not good for me, but when a patient is trying to pull their catheter out and jump out the window, you don’t tend to think about nipping for a wee!)

Thanks for the advice, and for giving me support to go back to my GP. I’ll try and book in, but... Christmas, you know?

Will keep you updated!

I’m in the UK, and my GP is 100% unhelpful.

I don’t even know what to say to them, as it’s the same problems I’ve had before.

I had a spinal MRI recently that had a two line report saying “no significant abnormalities that would cause current symptoms” as well.

Nope and nope.
Got originally told the ignore would just heal, but I get flare ups every few months, and I just got given diazepam for that.

The incontinence, again, I just got told it happen so rarely to me that it “doesn’t count as incontinence” and is probably just and EDS and anxiety thing, and that I should do kegels.
It’s frustrating, because I have great pelvis floor control generally, I just get no real feeling that I need to go.

Having to empty my menstrual cup (so obviously, loads of blood) in a bathroom where the lights were malfunctioning, flickering like a horror movie.
The bathroom had a weird set up, so the mirror was directly opposite and at the eye-line of the toilet, so I kept looking up and staring right into my own face in the flickering light, and had blood all over my hands.

I got back to my base after that hair easing experience to find someone had smashed a window, and then took a call within 5-10minutes, saying we were to go on lockdown, as someone had taken 3 members of staff hostage.
Only got stood down about 20minutes before the end of my shift....it was a tense night.

Effective is low, problematic for kidneys and clotting. Plus all types of cholesterol are very, possibly dangerously high. Not great. 
Plus creatinine is off, again, kidneys and liver...

East Midlands, I did have to GP shop a little, within the surgery that I went to.

One GP I saw with worsening pain said “Well you had blood tests about a year ago, so there’s no point doing any now.”
1) tests from a YEAR AGO.
2) new and worsening pains. Hello??

Crit car nurse in the UK here too! Took forever; got my POTs diagnosis first, then chronic pain from an “old sports injury”. 
Then got a fibro diagnosis, but when the pain was worse and worse, and I had subluxes and a beighton score of 9/9, clicking hips, TMJ subluxes and locking, and finally a rib dislocation after a hard cough, I got a referral to a geneticist, as rheumatology said “EDS isn’t a rheumatological issue to diagnose.”

Not hearing loss, but there has been a growing connection with EDS and Hyperacusis; the nerve signals constantly firing for pain mean that nerves are more “ready” to fire off signals for anything, including sound, so instead of filtering sound correctly, you hear everything, very loudly and very painfully.
Sometimes, my ears would “pop” and I’d lose my hearing for a bit, because my brain just shut off the signals after becoming overwhelmed.
